set.pl: Her house stood on the north part of lots 6-7, block 3, Burns, Farnam and Burns' Addition, on the W side of S. 6th St between Jay and King Sts, next to the First Baptist Church (which bought the south 55 ft). Today the spot is church-owned land on the 5th-6th / Jay-King block.

set.t: Urban lot, now church property and paved: look only.
set.st: Mary Ann Parker came to La Crosse in 1855 with a wealthy husband who soon died. She drew her money (several thousand dollars) out of the banks, nailed up the windows of her mansion and lived as a recluse for over 40 years among some of the finest homes in the city; the general opinion was that she had money buried around her rickety house. She died Aug. 25, 1901, aged 82. Her will left most of an estate of nearly $15,000 to the First Baptist Church and was upheld in November 1901 against Brooklyn relatives. Forum posters say her house and seven others are now a bank and parking lot. LiDAR cache check: City lot in La Crosse; paved over, LiDAR cannot help. Her probate inventory (Nov 1902) lists the house lot but no cash or personal estate. Her 1901 will was contested in a three-day trial in 1902; the estate inventory lists only the house lots next to the Baptist church and no cash.
